inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K (cop-20251231.htm): share-based compensation expense 336 (XBRL AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense) plus 100 net cash outflow on 'Issuance of company common stock' (financing), which for COP is net-share-settlement tax withholding net of option proceeds (FY24 78, FY23 52). No combined company figure is published, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases 5,018 (cash flow statement); H1-2026 3,006, with the quarterly pace doubled to $2.0bn in Q2 2026. Genuine repurchaser: the flat count is funded, and buybacks are value-neutral in this model (SBC is expensed).
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,201.3m shares outstanding at 30 June 2026 (Q2-2026 10-Q cover) plus ~1m dilutive options/RSU/PSU (EPS note) = 1,203m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The FY2024 jump (1,181m -> 1,275m) was the all-stock Marathon Oil acquisition, closed Nov-2024; no further non-SBC issuance is modelled.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Total debt 23,290 at 30-Jun-2026 (short-term 462 + long-term 22,828; includes ~0.8bn finance leases) less cash 6,574, short-term investments 1,118 and long-term debt securities 1,158 (AFS 1,613 total less 455 short-term) = 14,440. Operating leases (0.95bn) are excluded: under US GAAP their cost is already inside operating expense and hence EBITDA.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 for a large-cap E&P -> cost of equity ~9.3%; pre-tax debt ~5.2% (A-rated), ~35% blended tax -> ~3.4%; market-value weights ~87/13 -> WACC ~8.5%, rounded up to 9.0% for the depleting-asset nature of reserves. Same 9.0% on all three scenarios: commodity risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A. US GAAP: operating-lease cost already sits in opex/EBITDA; finance leases (~0.8bn) are in total_debt and their principal (175/yr) is NOT deducted from the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. ProfitLoss equals NetIncomeLoss (no material noncontrolling interest).
inputs.equity_affiliates_treatment: APLNG (47.5%), Qatar NFE/NFS and other equity affiliates (8.8bn carrying value) stay IN the flows: their equity earnings are inside 'total revenues and other income' and their distributions inside OCF. They are therefore NOT added to the bridge (would count them twice).
inputs.interest_income_treatment: COP is net debt, so interest_income is 0 per the house rule. The EBITDA margin path is nevertheless calibrated EX interest income (FY25 311m) so the cash netted against debt in net_debt is not also earning inside the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF, component build (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, cyclical'). COP is a pure-play upstream price-taker; single-year FCF swings 18.2bn (FY22) to 0.1bn (FY20) on the oil price, so FY0 is FY2025 (~$65 WTI, close to the $65-70 mid-cycle deck) and the driver paths do NOT extrapolate the 2026 oil rally that lifted H1-2026 revenue +14% YoY. FY2025 calibration: pretax 12,656 + interest and debt expense 855 + DD&A 11,500 - interest income 311 + SBC 336 = adj EBITDA 25,036 (42.5%); DD&A 19.5%; capex and investments 12,553 (21.3%); cash taxes 4,822 (36.5% of EBIT; FY23 33%, FY24 26%). Capex for FY2023-FY2025 and H1-2026 was missing from core_metrics (custom cop: XBRL tag) and was backfilled via make fix from the 10-K/10-Q cash flow statements. Terminal cap 12x (cyclical, depleting reserve base), Gordon at 9%/1.5% would be ~13.5x, so the cap binds in base.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle production growth (Lower 48 + Willow first oil 2029 + LNG ramp) at a flat real price deck
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (10.3% 3y / 16.7% 5y) diverges >30% from revenue (-9.1% / +25.7%) and EPS (-24.2% / n.m.). None of these is a growth rate: the 3y window runs from the FY2022 price peak, the 5y window from the FY2020 COVID trough (negative EPS and owner FCF, so 5y EPS/FCF CAGRs are undefined), and equity growth is inflated by two all-stock acquisitions (Concho 2021, Marathon Oil 2024).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes): FY20 ~-102, FY22 ~17,728, FY25 6,807. SBC is small (0.4-0.6% of revenue) and the owner/reported gap is ~6%, so the SBC adjustment does not change the growth story; the price cycle does.

base.growth_rationale: FY26 +6% banks part of the H1 price strength net of the $5bn non-core disposal programme (completed Jul-26); FY27 -2% reverts to a ~$65-70 WTI mid-cycle deck; FY28-30 +3-4% is Willow first oil (early 2029) and Port Arthur/Qatar LNG ramps; fading to 2% as Lower 48 matures.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY25 42.5% ex interest income, pre-SBC (FY23 44.4%, FY24 43.2%, FY19 44.7% on the same basis). Rises 0.5pp/yr to 45% on the >$1bn incremental run-rate cost target by YE26 and Marathon synergies; not credited with the full '$7bn FCF by 2029' plan.
base.capex_rationale: FY26 guidance $12.0-12.5bn = ~19.5% of revenue; Willow spend ($8.5-9.0bn gross) peaks FY26-28 then capex steps down to ~18%, converging on D&A (sustaining, depletion-replacement capex) by the terminal year.
base.cash_tax_rationale: 34%: FY23 33%, FY24 26%, FY25 36.5% of EBIT; high-tax Norway/Libya barrels keep it above US statutory.

scenario_narratives.base: Oil settles back into a $65-70 WTI / ~$4 Henry Hub mid-cycle after the 2026 rally. COP delivers the incremental $1bn cost target and holds the Marathon synergies, so margins edge back to the ~45% EBITDA it earned on comparable decks in FY19 and FY23. Willow reaches first oil in early 2029 near its revised $8.5-9.0bn budget and Port Arthur/Qatar LNG ramp on a months-not-years delay, adding 3-4%/yr of revenue through FY2030 before Lower 48 maturity slows growth to ~2%. Capex falls from the Willow peak to sustaining levels roughly equal to DD&A.
scenario_narratives.bull: A structurally tighter market - LNG demand outrunning the Qatar/US Gulf supply wave and OPEC+ spare capacity absorbed - keeps realised prices near $75-80 WTI. Lower cost structure plus price torque lifts EBITDA margin to ~48% (FY22-type conversion without FY22 prices), Willow and the LNG projects come on schedule, the FCF breakeven falls to the low-$30s as guided, and capex intensity drops to ~17.5% of revenue.
scenario_narratives.bear: OPEC+ unwinds spare capacity into non-OPEC growth (Guyana, Brazil, US shale) and WTI falls to ~$55 from 2027: revenue drops ~12% and margin compresses to ~39-40% as fixed North Slope and oil-sands costs deleverage. Willow runs over budget again and slips, Tier-1 Permian inventory depletes faster than assumed so maintenance capex stays near 19.5% of revenue, and growth fades to ~1%. The balance sheet (A-rated, ~0.6x net debt/EBITDA) survives this comfortably; it is a value case, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (up from the 15% default): COP is a pure-play price-taker with no downstream buffer, and the analysis flags loosening supply (OPEC+ spare capacity, non-OPEC growth) as the prevailing 2025-26 backdrop. Base 50%: the mid-cycle deck is also management's own planning basis ($70 WTI). Bull 25% (down from 35%): it needs a sustained price regime above mid-cycle, which COP cannot control, on top of flawless Willow/LNG execution.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the barrels at a mid-cycle price, not at today's print. The owner-FCF build normalises FY2025 (a ~$65 WTI year) and grows it with volume and cost-out, so the valuation is deliberately insensitive to where oil sits on the valuation date. When the share price runs ahead of this number, the market is capitalising an above-mid-cycle oil price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Oil and gas price: every ~$5/bbl WTI moves revenue ~6-8% and, with high operating leverage, owner FCF considerably more
Willow cost and schedule (already raised to $8.5-9.0bn, first oil early 2029) and Alaska/federal permitting litigation
Qatar NFE/NFS and Port Arthur LNG timing, which drive the FY2028-30 growth leg
Lower 48 Tier-1 inventory depletion raising sustaining capex above ~18% of revenue
Terminal cap at 12x owner FCF binds in the base case; a lower exit multiple for a depleting asset would cut value further
